text: Abhed is Zybuu's first product: a deep agent harness.
A harness is everything around the model. The loop. The tool contracts. The permission engine. The sandbox. The record. Change the harness, and the same model becomes a different product.
Abhed runs where your data is. One static binary, from a laptop to an air-gapped rack, with a signed offline bundle for the rack.
It runs any model. Twenty providers over three wire formats, including the one on your own GPUs. Changing vendors is a line of configuration, not a migration.
Every action is sandboxed by default, inside a boundary the operator sets and the agent cannot lift. Deny rules are absolute: no mode, no plugin, and no profile can widen what an operator forbade.
Writes are a permission, not a default. A change waits for a person, and the decision is recorded with who made it. When nobody is there to ask, the answer is no.
Every action is on the record: an append-only event log, replayable step by step, and exportable as OpenTelemetry traces into the tools you already run.
It embeds without weakening. The Go S D K gives your own software the same loop with the same guarantees, and structured output returns validated JSON, not prose.
Parallel subagents work in isolated git worktrees, so two writers can never collide. Scheduled runs turn recurring work into sessions on the record.
Extend it without forking it: extensions that can veto but never permit, skills, M C P servers, and custom providers.
Five ways to run it, one set of rules: interactive, headless, JSON, R P C, and a multi-user server with a web console.
And what Abhed does not do, said plainly. No certifications yet. No S L A. A human red team still outstanding. Everything else, it proves in its own test suite.
Abhed. The agent harness for work that cannot leave the building.
